title: Load Balancing
overview: Load balancing distributes incoming requests across multiple servers to ensure no single server becomes a bottleneck. It improves system availability, fault tolerance, and enables horizontal scaling of infrastructure. A load balancer sits between the client and the server pool, routing each request to the most appropriate backend based on a configured algorithm.
keyPoints: Distributes traffic evenly across multiple servers
Improves system availability and fault tolerance
Enables horizontal scaling of backend services
Can operate at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP) or Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS)
Provides health checks to route away from failed servers
Supports session persistence (sticky sessions) when needed

concepts.name: Round Robin
concepts.description: Sequentially routes requests to each server in turn. Simple and fast, but ignores server capacity and current load. Best for homogeneous server pools.

concepts.name: Weighted Round Robin
concepts.description: Like round robin, but assigns more traffic to higher-capacity servers based on configured weights. Good when servers have different hardware specs.

concepts.name: Least Connections
concepts.description: Routes to the server with the fewest active connections. Load-aware and adaptive, but adds overhead per request for tracking connection counts.

concepts.name: IP Hash
concepts.description: Uses client IP to determine the target server, ensuring the same client always reaches the same server (sticky sessions). Can cause uneven distribution if many users share an IP.

concepts.name: Random
concepts.description: Selects a random server for each request. Statistically approaches even distribution at scale with zero coordination overhead.

tools.name: HAProxy
tools.description: Open source, battle-tested, supports Layer 4 and Layer 7, excellent performance

tools.name: Nginx
tools.description: Lightweight, widely used in production, doubles as a reverse proxy and web server

tools.name: AWS ALB / ELB
tools.description: Fully managed AWS service with auto-scaling, SSL termination, and WAF integration

tools.name: F5 BIG-IP
tools.description: Enterprise-grade hardware/software solution with advanced security features

tradeoffs: Simple round-robin is fast but may be unfair under varying load. Sophisticated algorithms improve fairness and load distribution but add complexity and latency per request. Hardware load balancers offer extreme throughput but are expensive; software solutions like HAProxy are cost-effective for most workloads.
interviewTips: Always ask if the system needs sticky sessions — this affects algorithm choice significantly
Distinguish between L4 (TCP) and L7 (HTTP) load balancing and when to use each
Health checks are critical — describe how the LB detects and routes around failures
Mention that the load balancer itself can be a SPOF — use active-passive or active-active HA pairs
